source.title: Deep Linear Networks can Benignly Overfit when Shallow Ones Do
source.authors: Niladri S. Chatterji; Philip M. Long

record.tranche_reason: Studies benign overfitting in deep linear and ReLU networks on noisy regression data, a different setting from the claim's random image-label and pixel-input tests.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random image labels, chance test error under random labels, shuffled or Gaussian-noise inputs, varying fractions of randomly corrupted labels, explicit regularization, or the order of learning real versus random labels. It cites prior work on fitting noisy data. Its own results measure excess risk as initialization scales and input dimension vary; those findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes interpolation and excess risk in regression with signal-dependent targets plus additive Gaussian noise. It does not test completely randomized labels, corrupted-label fractions, or fitting unstructured replacements for a training dataset. Gaussian covariates generated together with teacher-dependent targets do not establish V3. The record's T3 classification should therefore be changed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Under stated conditions, deep linear networks approach or match risk bounds for the minimum-norm interpolator. The authors also conclude that the conditional variance term is identical, so depth does not improve the handling of noise through that term. Simulations show initialization-dependent risk and a first-/last-layer asymmetry for ReLU networks.
record.recipe_differences: Analyzes deep linear and ReLU regression with additive Gaussian noise and excess-risk bounds or measurements, rather than random-label image classification and training/test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Excess risk changes with first- and last-layer initialization scales in deep linear networks; in ReLU networks it increases with first-layer scale and is largely unaffected by final-layer scale. Small initialization can bring the deep linear solution close to the minimum ℓ2-norm interpolator.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep linear networks have greater excess risk at large first- or last-layer initialization scales; small scales produce solutions closer to the minimum-norm interpolator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale affects excess risk and proximity to the minimum-norm solution in the studied deep linear regression setting.

fits_no_version.finding: ReLU networks' excess risk increases with first-layer initialization scale and is largely unaffected by final-layer scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: First- and final-layer initialization scales have different effects on excess risk in the studied ReLU regression setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 7 reports training the simulated linear and ReLU networks until squared training loss falls below 1e-7, using full-batch gradient descent with step size 1e-4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The studied networks interpolate synthetic teacher-generated regression targets with additive Gaussian noise.

record.problems: The reported simulation results are plotted rather than numerically tabulated in the supplied text. Simulations average 20 runs and report 95% confidence intervals; the text does not provide exact plotted values.

untested.parts: Completely randomized training labels, chance-level test performance, and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels, and convergence across corrupted-label fractions.
Fitting shuffled, independently permuted, or Gaussian-noise replacements for structured inputs with the same networks.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across randomly corrupted-label fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared signal and memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Near-zero regression training loss is reported, but it does not establish fitting completely randomized labels. No verdicts on V1–V6 are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random labels, image classification, training error and test error at chance.
Training time for true versus random labels and convergence as the fraction of corrupted labels changes.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across fractions of randomly corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.
